institutions.regulator: CFPB, with bank regulators such as the OCC and FDIC

depositInsurance.value: Up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category (FDIC)

institutions.retirementSystem: Social Security, plus workplace 401(k) plans and individual IRAs
institutions.unemploymentNote: State unemployment insurance usually replaces part of your wages, often around 40–50%, for up to about 26 weeks. Rules differ by state.

cashAtHome.name: Cash at home
cashAtHome.note: Loses value to inflation and can be lost or stolen.

everydayAccount.name: Checking account
everydayAccount.note: For your paycheck and debit card, usually little or no interest.

savingsAccount.name: High-yield savings account
savingsAccount.note: Interest roughly follows the Fed rate; FDIC-insured at insured banks.

indexFund.name: Broad stock index fund
indexFund.note: Owns small pieces of hundreds of companies. Value goes up and down; long-term average historically positive.

retirementProduct.name: 401(k) with employer match
retirementProduct.note: Paid in from your paycheck before tax. Many employers add a match. Early withdrawals before age 59½ usually cost a 10% penalty plus tax.

informalSavings.name: Lending circle
informalSavings.description: Friends or community members each pay in a fixed amount every month and take turns receiving the pot, a tradition in many immigrant communities (tandas, susus, huis). Some nonprofits run lending circles that report payments to credit bureaus.

bigLifeEvent.name: A wedding
bigLifeEvent.note: Weddings are among the largest costs young couples face, and are often partly paid for with credit cards.

culture.familySupport: A family member back home needs help with a medical bill
notes: Your FICO credit score affects renting an apartment, loans, and sometimes car insurance.
Many workplaces match 401(k) contributions; not taking the match leaves part of your pay on the table.

scams.message: Toll Services: You have an unpaid toll of $6.99. Pay today to avoid a $50 late fee: ezpass-tollpay.info
scams.tell: Fake unpaid-toll texts are one of the most common US scams. Toll agencies don't text links to pay; check your account on the official site.

scams.message: You owe back taxes. Pay $1,800 today with gift cards or a warrant will be issued for your arrest.
scams.tell: The IRS contacts you by mail first and never demands gift cards or threatens immediate arrest by phone.

scams.message: Oops! I sent you $500 on Zelle by mistake. Can you please send it back to this number?
scams.tell: The 'mistaken payment' is often stolen or fake. Don't send money back yourself; contact your bank.

scams.message: Remote job: earn $300/day rating products online. Deposit $100 in crypto to unlock your first tasks.
scams.tell: Real jobs never ask you to pay to start. 'Task' jobs ask for bigger and bigger deposits.

scams.message: Direct deposit received: $1,604.22 from ACME Logistics payroll.
scams.tell: A notification inside your own banking app, with no link or request, is normal.

scams.message: Did you attempt a $48.20 purchase at a grocery store? Reply YES or NO. We will never ask for your PIN or password.
scams.tell: A yes/no fraud check that asks for no codes or links is a normal bank alert. If unsure, call the number on your card.
